newsitem.title: USA: Oscar-winning actor Jimmy Stewart dies, aged 89.
newsitem.headline: Oscar-winning actor Jimmy Stewart dies, aged 89.

text.p: Oscar-winning actor Jimmy Stewart, a gangly, slow-speaking, reluctant American hero who starred in such classics as "Mr. Smith Goes To Washington" and "It's A Wonderful Life," died on Wednesday, his agent said. He was 89.
Mort Viner, his agent, said Stewart died of cardiac arrest at his home in Beverly Hills. He was one of the greatest stars of Hollywood's golden era.

Stewart won Hollywood's biggest accolade, an Oscar, for best actor opposite Katharine Hepburn in "The Philadelphia Story" in 1940. In 1980 he was given an award for lifetime achievement by the American Film Institute and in 1984, another honorary Oscar.
Stewart, known to Hollywood as Jimmy but the rest of the world as James, played in 80 films during his career, and was nominated four more times for Academy Awards.
One of Hollywood's biggest stars at the peak of his career, critics sometimes complained he always played James Stewart, the small-town boy.
But behind his mannerisms lay years of hard training, perfecting what other actors, such as Cary Grant, and directors, like the late John Ford and Alfred Hitchcock, called a formidable technique.
"He played himself, but he played the character," Ford said of Stewart. "He was good in anything."

A small-town boy from Pennsylvania who never lost his quiet courtesy, Stewart was earning $3,000 a week as a movie star in 1941 when he enlisted in the then-U.S. Army Air Corps as a private for $21 a month.

Stewart won the Distinguished Flying Cross, the Air Medal, the French Croix de Guerre and ended the war as a colonel. Always the reluctant hero, he refused all the publicity the military wanted to pour on him, insisting on being treated like any other serviceman.

Receiving the life achievement award of the American Film Institute in 1980, he told a star-studded audience: "I give you James Stewart, a remarkably fortunate fellow. This award ties a ribbon round a lifetime of letting me get paid for what I liked to do."

At the age of 80, Stewart, his hearing almost gone and needing strong spectacles, waged a campaign against studios adding colour to black and white films, including the Christmas season classic "It's A Wonderful Life."
The death of his wife, Gloria, in February 1994 hit Stewart hard. He rarely left his Beverly Hills home after that, his health deteriorated and friends said he continued grieving for years.
He was born James Maitland Stewart, of Scots-Irish descent, on May 20, 1908, in Indiana, Pennsylvania. "I sort of grew up in the hardware store," he once said.
In 1949 Stewart, then one of Hollywood's most eligible bachelors, married Gloria McLean, who had two sons by a previous marriage.
One, Ronald, was killed in the Vietnam War. Stewart always referred to him as "my son." Twin girls, Judy and Kelly, were born to the Stewarts on May 7, 1951.
